messages:
liam: FYI ran into ENI exhaustion during a CP split test. Shared-subnet mode allocated a bunch of ephemeral ENIs and hit ENILimitExceeded. Caused SNAT fallbacks and broke IP allowlists for a couple customers.

anya: Can you repro reliably? Need repro steps to draft a mitigation.

liam: Repro: 100 small tenants onboarding simultaneously, each created two bootstrap ENIs. AWS returned ENILimitExceeded within ~2m.

ross: Short-term: reduce parallelism on onboarding. Long-term: consider sticky tenant ENI pool to reuse addresses.

joan: Pool idea + LRU eviction sounds good. TTL 15-30m? Also add preflight quota check in rollout controller to pause if free_enis < threshold.

anya: Controller-level preflight is safer than manual. Metrics: free_enis, pool_hit_rate, alloc_rate. Console should show banner when paused.

liam: Proposed minimal plan: 1) controller preflight check, 2) tenant-shared ENI pool with LRU + 20m TTL + fast 5m reuse, 3) alert "eni_pool_low" when free < 15% for 5m, 4) add egress_id to logs. I'll write RFC.

joan: For Private deployments, note: customers manage ENIs themselves so document the difference.

infra-bot: infra-bot: New alert rule proposed: eni_pool_low. Pager: eng-oncall.

anya: Thanks. Also add CLI snippet to list ENI usage for triage.

liam: Will include. RFC tag: cp-eni-pool-backpressure. Drafting now.
